Housing Infrastructure Investment Fund 
Wicklow County Council welcomes the announcement from the Department of Housing, Local 
Government and Heritage of funding allocated to infrastructure projects supported in the first 
phase of the Housing Infrastructure Investment Fund (HIIF) programme. 
These projects are the first to be funded as part of a major multi-annual fund committed to 
unlocking land and enabling the delivery of housing at scale. These infrastructure projects will 
unlock housing in towns and cities across the country. 
Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage James Browne T.D. announced that three 
projects across within County Wicklow will receive support through this first phase: 
• 
Rathnew Inner Relief Road, between €10m and €20m. Directly unlocks lands for 418 
residential units and indirectly supports a further 186 residential units. 
 
• 
Fassaroe - Pedestrian & Cycle Bridge across N11/M11, Bray, < €10m. Bray MD and 
Environs LAP identifies capacity for 4,000 residential units in this area. The project also 
indirectly supports a further 3,000 residential units. 
 
• 
Fassaroe - Road Infrastructure N11 to Enniskerry, Bray > €20m. The Fassaroe LAP 
identifies capacity for 4,000 residential units in this area. The project also indirectly

Capital Assistance Scheme (CAS) 
Under CAS, the Department is accepting applications for capital funding for the delivery, through either

Assessment criteria

need of the CAS groups identified in the latest Social Housing Assessment, consultations with suitable local

Energy Retrofit Program 
As part of our ongoing Energy Efficiency retrofit programme, housing services are undertaking works across 
the county. This includes, depending on house surveyed, and not limited to external wall insulation, attic 
insulation, heat pumps and upgraded windows and doors. These works comply with our policy on energy 
fabric upgrades which went through the SPC in 2023. 
The driver of this programme is the improvement to energy efficiency of local authority properties (BER – 
B2 or better), energy cost savings and sustainability. The move from solid fuel to more sustainable, energy 
efficient and cost-effective heating systems contributes to the climate change agenda and dramatically 
improves the comfort levels of tenants in these properties. 
A new Framework has been developed and contracts are moving towards tender stage to deliver on 
projects in 2026, in line with DHLGH requirements.

The Homeless HAP Place finder provides assistance in:  
➢ seeking out potential properties suitable for households currently identified as homeless or at 
risk of homelessness;  
➢ liaising with specific households to establish their specific needs;  
➢ establishing relationships with local property agents and landlords; and,

➢ To date, 710 households (496 families & 212 singles) have been assisted under the Homeless 
HAP Scheme in Wicklow County Council from the inception on 1st October 2018 to 31st May 
2026. (276 homeless cases, 386 prevention cases to date and 48 direct provision).  178

Addressing Homelessness in Partnership with Approved Housing Bodies 
Homeless Supported Temporary Accommodation – Kilmantin Hill, Wicklow 
Kilmantin Hill has 11 rooms to support persons either homeless, exiting a higher support facility, or in danger 
of becoming homeless.  
There are 10 clients supported in the Kilmantin Hill facility, operated by Dublin Simon. There is continuous 
transition by the clients to suitable alternative accommodation. 
A report is being undertaken at present to cost the refurbishment of the current rooms with a view to making 
them all ensuite. More details will be available over the coming months. 
Homeless Family Service – Fitzwilliam Road, Wicklow   
Dublin Simon are engaged by Wicklow County Council to operate and manage the facility at Fitzwilliam 
Road, Wicklow as a Family Homeless Service. The building comprises of three 1-bed units, two 2-bed units, 
and two 3-bed units.  
It is envisaged that families will avail of the service for circa 6-months STA (Supported Temporary 
Accommodation) with key working support to enable families to transition from homelessness into 
Homeless HAP, or alternative longer-term accommodation.   
Homeless Supported Temporary Accommodation – San Remo, Bray 
San Remo is operated by Dublin Simon and incorporates a service model whereby there are a number of 
emergency/cold weather initiative beds and Supported Temporary Accommodation Beds (STA). There is 
on site key working support linking in with clients.    
The Neighbourhood Liaison Committee is now operational and meets monthly. 
Bi-monthly meetings are held with Dublin Simon and Wicklow County Council staff. 
Homeless Supported Accommodation - Carraig Eden, Greystones 
This facility provides 35 ensuite bedrooms with associated kitchens and common areas and is fully 
operational. Wicklow County Council run an in-reach service with the clients to support them as they 
continue their journey into more permanent accommodation.  
Other Homeless Supported Accommodation 
Wicklow County Council owned properties in Wicklow, Bray, and Greystones, leased to Approved Housing 
Bodies, provide 12 units of low to medium supported accommodation targeted to the particular support

Community Awards Scheme (CAS) 2026 
As part of its commitment to supporting local community development, Wicklow County Council operates 
an annual Community Award Scheme. 
The fund for 2026 will be available as grant aid to successful community groups and local organisations 
wishing to undertake community projects in their area.  
Maximum grant amount of €1,000.00 per organisation for small projects and group running costs. 
This year saw a significant increase in demand, with 309 grants approved this year compared to 215 last 
year an increase of approximately 44% and payments will issue shortly. 
 
Local Enhancement Programme (LEP) 2026 
This funding will provide capital supports that are essential for many small community groups and 
organisations, particularly those who serve disadvantaged communities in rural and urban areas. 
The scheme is designed to ensure local priorities are identified and met, to improve and enhance 
community facilities for all. Funding will be available to a diverse range of community groups including, but 
not limited to, community centres, parish halls and local voluntary groups. 
County Wicklow has received €199,043.66 as part of the Local Enhancement Programme 2026. 
The Wicklow Local Community Development Committee (LCDC) is responsible for allocating funding 
through this scheme. Applications must relate to one or more key priority areas identified in their LCDC's 
Local Economic and Community Plan (LECP) to be eligible for consideration. 
Applications are now closed and we are expecting an announcement from the Department of Rural and 
Community Development and the Gaeltacht in late June or early July 2026. 
 
 
IPB Pride of Place Competition 2026 
Wicklow County Council recently invited expressions of interest from local community groups who would 
like to be considered for nomination to the 2026 IPB Pride of Place Competition, delivered in partnership 
with Co-Operation Ireland.  
This much-loved annual all island competition, run in collaboration with local authorities, shines a spotlight 
on the incredible work happening in communities across Ireland. It celebrates the people who roll up their 
sleeves, work together, and make their local communities vibrant, welcoming, and inspiring places to live.

Maternal Mental Health 
Maternal mental health is a key focus during May, with Healthy Wicklow providing funding to support 
targeted community initiatives. This funding will enable the delivery of the Minding Mums Programme in 
The Colour Club every Thursday throughout May, offering a supportive space for mothers to connect, 
share experiences, and access wellbeing resources. In addition, a Buggyfit Programme will be delivered 
in Carnew every Monday throughout May, promoting physical activity and social engagement for new 
mothers in an inclusive setting.  
 
Food Poverty 
First of three cooking/shopping/budgeting events was held in Rathdrum Library.  There were 21 people in 
attendance.  Collaboration between HSCLS, KWETB, MABS, CIC and Healthy Food Made Easy was 
achieved.  There was very good feedback from participants.  The next Event is in The Little Flower Hall 
Bray on 12th May 2026 from 10-12.30.

Running every Friday in May (1st, 8th, 15th, 22nd & 29th) in The Colour Club, Arklow from 16:30–17:30, 
this series will gently guide participants through: 
• 
Building a positive mindset 
• 
Strengthening resilience 
• 
Managing stress & exam anxiety 
• 
Simple breathwork techniques they can use anytime, anywhere 
 
Each session gives teens practical tools to stay grounded and clear headed in the lead up to exams. 
Slaintecare Healthy Communities-Bray                                       
 
1. Children’s Wellness Hub 
The evaluation of the Children’s Wellness Hub is now complete, following almost two years of work between 
Mary Immaculate College and multiple local stakeholders. This evaluation provides a strong evidence base 
for the work being delivered in Bray and highlights the importance of trusted, community-based early 
intervention supports for children and families.

The project has now entered its second year of SEED funding, with a further €75,000 secured to support 
continued development. The Hub continues to expand, with three staff now employed and workshops 
ongoing with both children and parents. Planning is underway for a formal launch of the evaluation findings 
in early September, involving key stakeholders, services, organisations, and Wicklow County Council. 
2. Bray Traveller Project 
The Bray Traveller Project continues to progress positively and is meeting its key objectives under the 
current phase of Genio funding. The Housing Accommodation Officer role is now well embedded and 
continues to support Traveller individuals and families across housing advocacy, homelessness, tenancy 
sustainment, repairs, and wider wellbeing initiatives. 
Key areas of progress include: 
➢ 16 transfer cases currently being worked on, including overcrowding and medical priority cases 
➢ 4 trailer loan applications progressing 
➢ 54 individuals currently not housed, with ongoing support around applications and emergency 
accommodation 
➢ 6 new social housing applications submitted during this period 
➢ 18 homelessness cases, including 6 without secure accommodation, with active interagency 
engagement ongoing 
➢ Continued progress on housing repairs, insulation, disability adaptation works, and refurbishments 
following fire damage 
3. Period Poverty Initiative 
The Healthy Communities Period Poverty Initiative has now secured funding for 2026. This funding will 
support the continued provision of free menstrual products through community organisations and services 
working with vulnerable individuals and families in Bray. It will also support the delivery of targeted menstrual 
health education workshops within disadvantaged communities, helping to promote awareness, dignity, and 
longer-term wellbeing. At present, at least four workshops / talks are being planned across community 
settings and secondary schools in Bray. 
4. Food Poverty Research Project / Family Food Skills Pilot 
As part of the Sláintecare Healthy Communities Programme, a community food and nutrition research 
project is now underway in Bray. The purpose of this work is to build community-informed evidence to 
support future local interventions, planning, and policy responses in relation to food poverty, food insecurity, 
and nutrition. 
Alongside this, Sláintecare Healthy Communities has submitted a funding application with Bray & North 
Wicklow Area Partnership under the New Solutions Innovation Fund Programme for a new Bray Family 
Food Skills Pilot. 
This proposed pilot aims to build on the success of Healthy Food Made Easy by addressing a key barrier 
identified by participants: the difficulty of continuing to cook healthy meals at home due to food cost, limited 
equipment, and lack of confidence. The pilot proposes a whole-family model, combining:

The Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant is a payment you can get if you are turning a vacant house or building into 
your permanent home or a rental property.  The grant applies to qualifying vacant properties in cities, towns, villages and 
rural parts of the country.

Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant of up to €50,000 
• 
Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant including the Derelict Property top up grant of up €70,000 
To qualify for the top up of €20,000, an independent report prepared by a Structural Engineer, along with a copy of their 
Professional Indemnity Insurance, is required to be submitted along with the application, confirming, to the satisfaction of 
the local authority, that the property is derelict i.e. structurally unsound and dangerous. 
To qualify for the grant, applicants must: 
Have proof of ownership or evidence of active negotiations to buy the property (that is, confirmation of engagement from 
the estate agent or owner of the property) where you are seeking approval in principle for a grant. 
- 
Live in the property as your principal private residence or make it available for rent. 
- 
Have proof that the property has been vacant for at least 2 years and that it was built up to and including 2007.

communities. 
This year's theme is "Courage". 
In Ireland, courage takes many forms. It can mean navigating unfamiliar systems, learning a new language, building a life 
in a new country, finding employment, or helping children settle into new schools and communities. It is the determination 
to begin again despite uncertainty and challenge. 
Courage is also demonstrated by those who offer support, friendship, and welcome. It is shown by volunteers giving their 
time, sports clubs opening their doors, neighbours reaching out, families offering practical support, and communities 
standing up for fairness, dignity, and inclusion. Sometimes courage is found in simple everyday actions – offering a smile, 
sharing a conversation, inviting someone to join a local activity, or helping a newcomer feel that they belong. 
As an organisation, we recognise that providing protection to people fleeing conflict, persecution and hardship reflects 
our shared values of respect, dignity, equality, and compassion. Supporting those in need of protection is not only a 
humanitarian responsibility but also a reflection of the kind of inclusive and welcoming society we aspire to build. 
Refugee Week Ireland celebrates these everyday acts of courage by individuals, families, and communities across the 
country. Through sharing food, music, stories, conversation, and learning, it highlights both the courage it takes to seek 
safety and the courage it takes to be welcoming.

Operations

The IT Helpdesk continues to streamline the workflow for the technical support team with an average of 50 tickets

GIS & Systems Analysis 
Statutory Mapping & Local Area Plans 
 
• 
Continued work on the Council's statutory mapping programme, including detailed quality assurance checks on 
zoning datasets used within the MyPlan planning system. Mapping for a number of Local Area Plans was finalised 
and uploaded, ensuring planning information remains accurate and up to date. This work supports future planning 
decisions and provides a reliable source of information for the public and stakeholders. 
Baltinglass Regeneration Project 
 
• 
Produced a range of maps to support the Baltinglass Town Centre Refurbishment Scheme (Phase 1A). Additional 
mapping information was provided in response to project queries and design requirements. This work supports 
the delivery of regeneration initiatives aimed at enhancing the town centre environment. 
Heritage – Placenames Project 
 
• 
Worked with the Heritage Section on a project to preserve and document minor placenames throughout County 
Wicklow. Discussions are ongoing regarding the integration of this information into the Council's GIS systems. 
The project has the potential to make valuable local heritage information more accessible to the public. 
Wicklow Fire Service GIS Support 
 
• 
Provided mapping support to Wicklow Fire Service in relation to an upcoming inter-agency training exercise. 
Detailed maps were prepared to assist planning and coordination activities. GIS information continues to support 
emergency planning and operational preparedness across the county. 
Agricultural Inspections Mobile App 
 
• 
Met with staff from Cavan County Council and Environment Section personnel to review a mobile application 
used for agricultural inspections. The discussions focused on streamlining field data collection and enhancing 
reporting processes. Collaboration with other local authorities helps identify best practice and improve service 
delivery.
